description of the invoices print-on-demand module: it integrates an ODF open document editor like LibreOffice:
a xml schema of the invoice datas/contents to be published is defined: an invoice has a "customer_name", a "customer_address" and "lines with a product_name, price and quantity", etc...

the "template author" creates an ODF "template" invoice document with LibreOffice, and with "example contents/data": a header with an example customer name, a table with an example product line, with a cells with example product name, price and quantity etc...
the author then creates a style "customer_name" and assigns it to the customer name header example, then makes the same for the "product name" example celle etc...

the effect of that in the (XML) ODF format generated by LibreOffice, is that the ODF element of the customer name header has a "style" attribute "customer_name", the ODF element of the product name example celle has a "name" (not style) attribute "product_name" etc...

a first XSLT scripts generates, from this template document, a second XSLT script replacing the styled and/or named example contents by xpath queries feeding the real content from an XML invoice document extracted from the web site database;
the second XSLT script is executed online by the PHP code of the site, to generate the final ODF document;
finally, the LibreOffice batch PDF converter is executed to convert the ODF document to the final PDF invoice.

wit-dom-shim : Developed this Rust/JS PoC : its goal is to enable an early replacement of wasm-bindgen by wit-bindgen in rust web frameworks like Yew: wit-bindgen solves the " intermediate glue layer issue described in this post" of wasm-bindgen. This glue increases the response time and resources consumption of in browser Rust/Wasm applications, like Yew applications, and so, slows down their adoption. The problem today is that, for such frameworks to switch to wit-bindgen, the browsers is expected to support WIT, which is not expected to come soon. So this shim brings an intermediate solution based on WIT resources concept, enabling a Rust/Wasm framework to switch to wit-bindgen whatever the browsers support of WIT, making this glue a thing from the past.
